one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Gujarat-based B2B manufacturer of compact ring-spun cotton yarns and value-added yarns (Eli Twist, compact slub, Lycra-blended, organic) supplying textile manufacturers, garment exporters and bulk purchasers from a single spinning facility at Gondal, Rajkot.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Shree Ram Twistex manufactures 100% cotton yarns - Compact Ring Spun and Carded Yarns (combed and carded) in counts Ne 8 to Ne 40 - plus value-added yarns such as Eli Twist (Siro) Ne 40/2, Compact Slub and Lycra-blended yarns, used in knitting and weaving for denim, terry towels, shirting, sheeting, sweaters, socks, bottom wear, home textiles and industrial fabrics. It operates exclusively B2B, selling to institutional buyers (textile manufacturers, garment exporters, bulk purchasers, fabric processors) via direct sales and a broker/agent network domestically, with opportunistic exports routed through merchant exporters. By-product income comes from cotton waste, FP bales, viscose-cotton mix yarn and open-end yarn.

group_structure.title: Group structure (subsidiaries / JV / related parties)
group_structure.body:
- Goldsun Ceramic Private Limited — Other directorship / venture promoted by promoter Bhaveshbhai Ramani: Only other Indian company directorship of the CMD
- Ravi Oil Refineries — Partnership of promoter Bhaveshbhai Ramani: Oil refining venture
- Ravi Solvex & Oil Industries — Partnership / venture promoted by promoter Bhaveshbhai Ramani: Oil refining venture
- Nano-Agor Foods Private Limited — Past association of promoter Bhaveshbhai Ramani: Former association
- Shree Ram Munchies (India) LLP — Venture promoted by promoter Nidhi Bhaveshbhai Kothari
- Shree Ram Elite Industrial Services LLP — Venture promoted by promoter Nidhi Bhaveshbhai Kothari
- Shree Ram Tradebiz (India) LLP — Venture promoted by promoter Nidhi Bhaveshbhai Kothari
- Tecfine Knittex LLP — Venture promoted by promoter Nidhi Bhaveshbhai Kothari
- Group Companies — None identified: Per Board's materiality policy dated May 09, 2025 (Ind AS 24 related-party basis), the company has no group companies as on the RHP date

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Cotton Compact Ring Spun and Carded Yarns:** Carded Yarn (Ne 8 to Ne 40), Combed Yarn (Ne 8 to Ne 40)
- **Value-added Yarns:** Eli Twist (Siro) Yarn Ne 40/2 (combed and carded), Compact Slub Yarn, Lycra-Blended Yarn, Organic Yarn
- **By-products and Others:** Cotton Waste, Viscose-Cotton Mix Yarn, FP Bales, Open-End (OE) Yarn

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- Knitting and weaving end-uses: denim, terry towels, shirting, sheeting, sweaters, socks, bottom wear, home textiles, industrial fabrics
- Domestic market (93.87% of FY25 net sales; sold across Gujarat, Rajasthan, West Bengal, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, Madhya Pradesh, Punjab and Dadra & Nagar Haveli)
- Exports through merchant exporters (6.13% of FY25 net sales; 28.46% in FY24 - opportunistic, not consistent year-on-year)
- Gujarat alone contributed 93.48% of FY25 and 87.72% of H1 FY26 revenue from operations

cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: Fully integrated spinning facility covering all stages from cotton bale procurement, cleaning, carding, combing, spinning and winding to final yarn packaging at a single location. Backward linkage: principal raw material (cotton bales) procured through a network of brokers from ginning mills and traders across Gujarat, Maharashtra, Haryana and Madhya Pradesh; 123 / 149 / 147 / 174 suppliers in H1FY26 / FY25 / FY24 / FY23, of which 6 suppliers associated for over four years contributed 45.47%, 70.68% and 42.01% of total purchases in H1FY26, FY25 and FY24-FY23 periods as stated. Five in-house TFO (two-for-one) twisting machines (procured May 2025, scheduled operational from July 2025) described as a significant step toward full vertical integration for value-added yarns (Eli Twist, Lycra-blended). Captive renewable power: 1.2 MW rooftop solar operational July 2024, 6.1 MW ground-mounted solar (5 MW commissioned) and a proposed 4.2 MW wind project. Forward linkage: exclusively B2B sales - domestic via direct sales to institutional customers plus a network of 8 third-party brokers and agents (as of September 30, 2025); all exports routed through merchant exporters. Named long-standing institutional customers include Welspun Living Limited and Jindal Worldwide Limited. Working capital: sanctioned pledge loan limit of Rs 2,000 lakhs from Axis Bank Limited against cotton bale inventory.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Product-mix shift toward value-added/organic yarn: Organic Yarn rose from 0.87% of gross sales in FY25 to 21.52% in H1 FY26, alongside EBITDA margin improvement from 8.57% (FY25) to 12.90% (H1 FY26)
- Seasonal working-capital cycle: buffer cotton-bale stock built during the October-March harvest at optimal prices, financed through pledge loans against inventory (Rs 2,000 lakh sanctioned limit, Axis Bank)
- Power-cost reduction from captive solar generation (rooftop 1.2 MW; average 10,62,500 units generated during July-December 2024, reducing monthly electricity expenses)
- Opportunistic export sales via merchant exporters during periods of low domestic demand - export share swings between 6.13% (FY25) and 28.46% (FY24) of net sales
- Volume trajectory: yarn production of 6,898.50 MT (FY23), 8,573.85 MT (FY24), 8,475.30 MT (FY25) and 4,286.92 MT (H1 FY26) against 9,855 MT/annum installed capacity

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Expand captive renewable power - 6.1 MW ground-mounted solar plus a proposed 4.2 MW wind project - to reduce reliance on grid electricity and considerably lower electricity expenses
- Repay and/or pre-pay Rs 1,489 lakh of borrowings from Net Proceeds to deleverage the balance sheet
- Fund working capital (Rs 4,400 lakh from Net Proceeds) to support seasonal buffer-stock cotton procurement
- Maintain dual-channel market coverage: direct sales plus broker/agent network domestically and merchant exporters for overseas markets, while staying focused on core yarn manufacturing

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The capex programme in the provided text is captive power rather than new spinning capacity: the company installed a 1.2 MW rooftop solar plant (operational July 2024, average generation 10,62,500 units over July-December 2024), has established a 6.1 MW ground-mounted solar power plant (of which 5 MW is installed and commissioned; total estimated cost Rs 2,223.55 lakh already deployed) and proposes a 4.2 MW wind power project (Rs 3,900 lakh from Net Proceeds) - all for captive consumption to cut electricity expenses at the Gondal facility. Historically, spinning capacity was expanded in 2020 by adding six compact ring-spinning machines (9,792 spindles), taking the plant from 17,952 to 27,744 spindles and yarn capacity from 5,500 to 9,855 MT/annum.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Modern European spinning machinery (Switzerland, Germany, Italy): compact spinning systems, high-speed autoconers, contamination clearers, electronic yarn clearers and automated vacuum systems integrated with real-time monitoring
- Climate-controlled, dust-free production environment with centralized air-conditioning and Swiss-made air filtration, preserving fibre integrity and yarn quality
- Long-standing institutional customer relationships (e.g. Welspun Living Limited, Jindal Worldwide Limited); 6 of the top customers served for more than four years
- Exclusive B2B model enabling customized yarn solutions on technical parameters (count, twist, strength) and efficient large-order fulfilment
- Established cotton procurement network of brokers, ginning mills and traders across Gujarat, Maharashtra, Haryana and Madhya Pradesh (123-174 suppliers per period), with buffer-stock strategy during the October-March harvest backed by a Rs 2,000 lakh pledge-loan limit from Axis Bank
- Zero Liquid Discharge facility design and captive renewable energy (1.2 MW rooftop solar operational July 2024; 5 MW of 6.1 MW ground-mounted solar commissioned) lowering power costs and carbon footprint
- Promoter-led management: founder-CMD with 14+ years of industry experience, supported by experienced KMP and senior management

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Customer concentration — Top 1 customer contributed 28.57% (H1 FY26), 32.97% (FY25), 44.35% (FY24) and 37.26% (FY23) of revenue; top 10 customers 77-86%; business is on purchase-order basis with no long-term contracts
- Geographic revenue concentration in Gujarat — Gujarat contributed 87.72% (H1 FY26), 93.48% (FY25), 83.14% (FY24) and 85.59% (FY23) of revenue from operations
- Single manufacturing facility — All production is at one facility in Gondal, Rajkot; any disruption there affects the entire output (9,855 MT/annum capacity)
- Raw-material dependence and supplier concentration — Single principal raw material (cotton bales) procured seasonally October-March; 6 long-associated suppliers contributed 45.47%, 70.68% and 42.01% of total purchases in H1 FY26, FY25 and FY24 respectively
- Working-capital intensity — Buffer cotton inventory must be carried through the year and is financed by pledge loans against stock (Rs 2,000 lakh sanctioned limit), exposing the company to inventory and funding-cost risk
- Inconsistent export channel — Exports are opportunistic and routed only through merchant exporters, so export revenue is not consistent year-on-year (6.51% FY23, 28.46% FY24, 6.13% FY25 of net sales)
- Reliance on commissioned industry report — Industry/market data is from a D&B report exclusively commissioned and paid for by the company for the Issue, which the DRHP itself flags as carrying inherent risks

commitments.title: Promises (RHP)
commitments.body:
- **Complete the 6.1 MW ground-mounted solar power plant for captive use (5 MW already installed and commissioned; total estimated cost Rs 2,223.55 lakh already deployed), with Net Proceeds funding a part of the project**
- **Set up a 4.2 MW wind power plant for captive use, funded with Rs 3,900 lakh from Net Proceeds, with deployment scheduled in Fiscal 2026**
- **Repay and/or pre-pay, in full or part, Rs 1,489 lakh of borrowings from the Net Proceeds during Fiscal 2026**
- **Deploy Rs 4,400 lakh of Net Proceeds into working capital - Rs 2,945 lakh in Fiscal 2026 and Rs 1,455 lakh in the following fiscal**
- **Reduce reliance on grid electricity and considerably lower electricity expenses through captive solar and wind capacity**

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Expand captive renewable power - 6.1 MW ground-mounted solar plus a proposed 4.2 MW wind project - to reduce reliance on grid electricity and considerably lower electricity expenses
- Repay and/or pre-pay Rs 1,489 lakh of borrowings from Net Proceeds to deleverage the balance sheet
- Fund working capital (Rs 4,400 lakh from Net Proceeds) to support seasonal buffer-stock cotton procurement
- Maintain dual-channel market coverage: direct sales plus broker/agent network domestically and merchant exporters for overseas markets, while staying focused on core yarn manufacturing
